A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Posterior-GRPO work. Text extraction and visual inspection cover the main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices sufficiently for reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original code-generation and mathematical evaluations, reward-model comparisons, ablations and a reasoning-quality correlation analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–3, the main figures and Appendices A.4–A.5.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same optimized/original/degraded preference pairs, Bradley-Terry reward-model training and outcome-gated thinking reward in P-GRPO. Equation 1 and the described training procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain DeepCoder-Preview and DAPO-Math-17k training and evaluations on HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), LiveCodeBench, BigCodeBench, LCB-RB, RewardBench, MATH500, Minerva Math and AIME2024. The revised 3B appendix chart introduces no new coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparators, as do the preference-pair and reward-model substitution studies. Table 3 shortens the GRPO and P-GRPO labels without changing the compared methods.

E3.justification: Model sizes, evaluation metrics, greedy decoding, benchmark subsets and training budgets match after accounting for relocation to the appendices. The revised chart concerns the already-described 3B ablation. Omission of the rollout count does not establish a changed setting.

E4.justification: V1's Figure 8, labeled as the 3B preference-pair ablation, duplicates its 7B Figure 5. V2's Appendix A.5 Figure 6 replaces that duplicate with distinct 3B results. Other ablations, training analyses, the reasoning example and correlation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the same chi-square analysis with p = 9.3e-15. Neither adds training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical comparisons of model performance.

E6.justification: The appendix ablation changes from duplicated 7B values, including an all-pair average near 82, to 3B values with an average near 70, consistent with Table 2's 69.84. Other pair-combination scores also change. Tables 1–3 and the main training curves remain unchanged; this is corrected reporting, not a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: The reward equation, preference-pair definitions and soft-reward formulation are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised. Corrected indices in Figure 2 are presentation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three contributions and claims about reward-model effectiveness, mitigating reward hacking, the 4.5% improvement over outcome-only RL and mathematical generalization.

C2.justification: The interpretations involving reasoning quality, preference-pair contrast, SFT versus RL and reward hacking remain substantively unchanged. Computational limitations and proposed longer-output and iterative-learning extensions are also retained.

D1.justification: V2 omits v1's statement that eight responses are sampled per problem for RL rollout. Its benchmark-generation prompt reference points to A.6, although the RL prompt is in A.3. Other hyperparameters, prompt contents, hardware information and the resource link are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to GRPO, outcome-based rewards, Evol-Instruct and reward-model benchmarks are retained. Expanded bibliographic details and added reference URLs do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: V2 condenses Experimental Setup and moves detailed baseline and benchmark descriptions into Appendices A.1–A.2. It adds section numbering and explicit appendix references, with limited copyediting and author-header changes; most prose and the overall narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column body with a single-column layout, revises Figures 1–3 and combines v1's Figures 4–6 into four-panel Figure 4. Tables and appendix displays are resized and rearranged. Figure 2 corrects repeated advantage labels, while Figure 3 removes reward-score annotations retained in the prose.

improvement.justification: Replacing the duplicated, misleading 3B appendix chart with results consistent with Table 2 improves the accuracy of the supporting evidence. Corrected diagram labels provide another limited benefit. These gains outweigh the modest reproducibility losses from omitting the eight-response rollout count and misdirecting a prompt reference; the central method and main results remain unchanged.
